Description: Croasdaile is a quiet, established community in northwest Durham known for its spacious homes, wooded lots, and relaxed suburban atmosphere. Many parts of the neighborhood are centered around the private Croasdaile Country Club, giving the area a classic golf-community feel with mature landscaping and winding streets. Residents value the peaceful setting and larger properties while still being only a short drive from downtown Durham and Duke University.
Notes: Lots of Colonial, Georgian and ranch houses on big lots.  Just north of  I-85 in NW Durham
Golf Notes: Course is well-maintained, more relaxed and neighborhood-oriented, less old-money prestige, but very solid golf and convenient location.  Good practice facilities, full amenities including pickleball

Description: A polished 1990s master-planned golf community where large homes, mature landscaping, and country-club amenities create a classic South Charlotte suburban lifestyle with easy access to the city’s best shopping in Southpark.
Notes: Drove around, very pretty area with hills and trees.  Suburban feel, near the Interstate. Estates, townhomes, and smaller homes.
Golf Notes: TPC Piper Glen golf course is a bit rough on the cart paths, pretty course.  Invited Club, no big waitlist.

Description: Vital urban style in a suburb of Raleigh. Fancy City park surrounded by Townhomes
Golf Notes: Prestonwood has multi-year wait.  20 min Drive to Brier Creek.

Description: A classic, upscale golf‑course community where mature trees, lakeside views, and elegant homes blend with country‑club social life and easy access to the best of Cary living.  Very close to Waverly Place shopping and WakeMed.
Notes: Very fancy, constant teardowns, mix of styles from mid-century to French chateau. MacGregor Lake only for the country club
Golf Notes: Long waitlist confirmed.  Lovely course.  Limited options in the area.  25 min to Brier Creek

Description: The Ballantyne area is an affluent, master-planned suburban community in south Charlotte developed on the historic Ballantyne Ranch in the 1990s. It features upscale homes, business and entertainment center. With manicured landscapes, top schools, and shopping at Ballantyne Village, it offers a polished, self-contained suburban experience.
Notes: Feels like Plano.  Has big suburban mixed use Ballentyne Bowl.
Golf Notes: Piper Glen (asphalt cart path) and Firethorn in Waxhaw are Invited clubs.   Don't think either has a waitlist.  Ballentyne is more popular, long wait.

Description: Upscale college town with UNC campus energy. Established 2000s hilly neighborhood with mature trees and a vibrant intellectual community.  Saw house here.
Notes: Chapel Hill offers a unique blend of academic prestige and Southern charm. Home to the University of North Carolina, the town maintains a youthful, intellectual atmosphere while preserving its historic character. The downtown area features locally-owned restaurants, bookstores, and the iconic Franklin Street. Neighborhoods range from historic homes near campus to newer developments with golf course access. The town prioritizes green space with an extensive trail system and well-maintained parks. Housing tends toward the premium side, reflecting the desirability of the area and excellent school system.

Description: Walkable urban neighborhood near downtown with shops & restaurants. Historic and new infill homes
Notes: Narrow streets, urban traffic and noise.  Vibrant engaged community, social district
Golf Notes: long wait, sky-high dues like DCC

Description: A charming suburban town southeast of Charlotte that has managed to preserve its small-town soul while growing into a desirable residential community.
Notes: The downtown district (have seen) offers alternative to typical strip malls: locally-owned shops, diverse restaurants, and the Matthews Farmers Market.  Novant and Atrium both here.   Median house price reflects smaller suburban homes
Golf Notes: 3+ year waitlist, 40k initiation at both Cedarwood and Providence

Description: Lochmere is a well-established planned community in the southwest part of Cary, known for its mature trees, lakes, and extensive walking trails. Built around several small lakes and a private golf club, the neighborhood has a quieter, more traditional suburban feel than many newer developments in the Triangle. Residents often highlight the greenways, community pools, and proximity to nature, including nearby Hemlock Bluffs Nature Preserve.
Notes: Variety of subdivisions and prices.  Nice housing styles.  Former country club provides neighborhood tennis courts & swimming.  Golf course is semi-private, no club.
Golf Notes: Next closest country club is Prestonwood.  McGregor Downs has a long waitlist.

Description: Older area of S Charlotte with plentiful trees & windy roads, mid-century and later homes
Notes: near Raintree & Providence Park neighborhood also; community pool or park; 15 min to southpark; shop at nearby Arboretum
Country Club Name: Providence Country Club, Raintree Country Club,  Ballantyne
Golf Notes: Providence & Ballantyne have waits.  Raintree may not.  $10-15k initiation.

Description: A historic, tree-covered country-club neighborhood started in the 1920s around Hope Valley Country Club where classic architecture, winding streets, and long-established homes create one of Durham’s most traditional and prestigious residential settings.
Notes: Gentrifying area, slope changes, mostly built in the 60s.  Parks are within  5-10 min drive, none in the neighborhood
Golf Notes: Haven't confirmed HV Wait list.  Popular, established course.   Croasdaile is 20 min away.

Description: A serene, quiet tree-lined neighborhood that blends upscale suburban living with immediate access to hiking, trails, and the natural beauty of Duke Forest.  Larger lots with a mid-century vibe.
Notes: Older, Architect-driven, funky neighborhood with rolling hills and lots of trees, south of the Duke campus. Split-level and ranch houses mixed in.
Golf Notes: No course in the neighborhood.  Would have to drive to a nearby course.

Description: Brier Creek is a modern, master-planned community in suburban northwest Raleigh. Located between Raleigh and Durham and just minutes from Research Triangle Park and Raleigh–Durham International Airport, the neighborhood is especially popular with professionals who commute around the Triangle. Brier Creek blends newer homes, townhouses, and apartments with major shopping and dining at Brier Creek Commons, while outdoor recreation is close by at William B. Umstead State Park
Notes: Toll Brothers home community built in the early 2000s.  Very suburban, but pleasant. 10 min from State Park
Golf Notes: No apparent waitlist, $10-15k initiation, under $1k dues, cart fee extra. Trying hard, chef is local
